narrative:
The model estimated your probability of bad credit at 33%, meaning roughly a one-in-three estimated chance that an applicant with a similar profile would run into credit difficulty. The lender treats that risk level as above its approval cutoff, so your application was denied.

The most influential item in the assessment was the presence of a guarantor. This was the strongest factor and it worked in your favour, since most approved applicants have no other debtor listed. The second most important item was your checking-account position: your account is recorded as overdrawn, whereas most approved applicants have no overdraft or a positive balance. This was the main adverse factor among the top three. The third most important item was the amount requested: at 1,755 DM, it is well below the approved average of about 3,020 DM, which also worked in your favour. The denial therefore reflects a mixed picture, with the checking-account signal carrying more weight than the positive signals from the guarantor and lower amount.

To improve your chances, bring your checking account into a positive balance and keep it there for several months, then ask the lender whether they can reconsider with updated account information. Keep your guarantor documentation current, and ask what specific balance or account history would meet their approval criteria.
